title: Writing the min loop
idea: TOOL: assemble the smallest-so-far loop, noticing it is the max loop with one sign changed.

exercises.prompt: Tap the tokens to start the smallest at the first value of nums.
exercises.explanation: best = nums[0] — the SAME safe start as the max loop. Only the comparison will differ.

exercises.prompt:
Write the loop header that visits each value in nums (call it n):

for ____ in nums:
exercises.explanation: 'for n in nums:' — identical to the max loop's header.

exercises.prompt:
Write the test that is true when n is smaller than the best so far:

    if n ____ best:
exercises.explanation: n < best is true when n is smaller — the flipped comparison that makes this a min.

exercises.prompt:
Write the line that saves the smaller value into best:

        best ____ n
exercises.explanation: best = n — the same save step as max. The winner goes INTO best.

exercises.prompt: Put the whole min program in order.
exercises.explanation: Start best, loop, test with <, replace on a smaller value, print. Compare to the max program: only the sign changed.

exercises.prompt: You assembled the loop for nums = [6, 2, 9, 4]. What prints?
exercises.explanation: best drops 6 -> 2 and nothing is smaller. It prints the minimum, 2.

exercises.prompt: You have a working max loop on screen. What is the fastest way to make it a min loop?
exercises.explanation: One character. That is the whole point of this unit — the pattern transfers.

exercises.prompt: Where must 'best = n' sit so it only runs on a smaller value?
options: At the same level as the for
exercises.explanation: Indent it under the if so the replace only happens on a win — exactly like max.

exercises.prompt: The min loop and the max loop have the same number of lines.
exercises.explanation: They are the same loop structure. Only the comparison sign inside the if is different.

exercises.prompt: Before trusting your min loop, what should you do?
options: Trace a small list by hand and compare to the output
exercises.explanation: Hand-trace a small list to get the expected smallest, then check the code matches — the Check habit.
